subject: Request: Renewal bridge authority & term-reset for Curbside
messages:
From: James Reynolds <james.reynolds@curbside.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Trent <olivia.trent@curbside.com>, procurement@curbside.com
Date: Wed, 1 May 2029 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions + ask for flex on terms

Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We appreciated the improved latency on the new model bundle; it materially helped a couple of our flows. That said, as we approach the contract renewal for our enterprise plan (May 31), our finance team ran the numbers and the delta to the new pricing tier is larger than expected.

Two specific asks from our side: 1) can Redwood provide a one-time credit to offset our Q2 overage (our usage spiked due to a seasonal campaign), and 2) we need flexibility to move our billing to an annual, calendar-aligned term (term reset) so renewals sync with our fiscal year.

If there's a standard bridge/credit package you can apply to close this, please let me know what authority is required. I can pull together the procurement paperwork quickly. I attached the Q1 usage report.

Appreciate it —
James Reynolds
VP Product
Curbside Technologies

Attachment: usage_report_q1.csv
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: James Reynolds <james.reynolds@curbside.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal questions + ask for flex on terms

James — thanks for the note and for the usage file. I'm looping in Kimberly (sales lead for Renewals) and Marissa (Customer Success lead) to make sure we capture the operational impact.

Short answer: we have a precedent for a one-time makegood credit and for aligning terms, but approvals depend on the concession level. Can you share the target credit amount (ballpark) and whether Curbside is willing to commit to a 12-month renewal on the adjusted annual billing? If you can sign for 12 months we can be more flexible on the credit and include an SLA addendum.

I'll start an internal request for authority once we have numbers.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Request: Renewal bridge authority & term-reset for Curbside

Team — forwarding Curbside's request. Quick summary of internal thinking:

- Account health: CS reports strong product adoption but usage variability due to campaign spikes; renewal uplift likely but risk of churn if costs jump too fast.
- Commercial ask: 1) one-time credit to offset Q2 overage (~$42k requested by finance), 2) term reset to align to calendar year, 3) optional SLA add-on (they want 99.95% for the next 12 months).

Proposed internal concession package (what I think we can ask authority for):
- One-time credit: $30k (below their current ask) if Curbside signs a 12-month commitment at the new tier.
- Term reset: yes, effective 6/1/2029 to 5/31/2030, billing aligned annually.
- SLA addendum: include 99.95% target with standard service credits (capped).

This exceeds my on-hand discount authority (>20% effective concession), so I'm requesting executive approval for: 1) increase credit to $40k (to meet in the middle), and 2) allow the SLA addendum with a one-time commitment credit.

Attachments: proposed_amendment_v3.pdf (draft amendment with term language and SLA clause).

Kimberly
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

Kimberly — I validated the usage spike and the operational asks with the implementation team. Notes:

- The spike was caused by an A/B test that ran for three weeks; they exceeded committed throughput on several endpoints. Usage profile suggests this was one-time but could repeat during Q4 marketing pushes.
- SLA impact: engineering is comfortable adding a 99.95% SLA addendum for the next 12 months; we should include a small ramp clause to let our cache warm (30 days).
- Risk: if we give a credit that's too large without a firm 12-month commitment we set a precedent for other similar mid-market accounts.

Recommendation: approve a $40k one-time credit contingent on DocuSign-signed 12-month renewal at the new tier and inclusion of the SLA addendum (with 30-day ramp). This matches Kimberly's ask for exec approval and keeps the net concession moderate.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: ceo@redwood.ai, cfo@redwood.ai, head_of_revenue@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 May 2029 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: EXEC AUTH REQUEST — Approve $40k credit + term reset + SLA addendum for Curbside (deal CRB-2029-0427)

Folks — requesting executive sign-off on a one-time concession package to preserve renewal for Curbside Technologies. Details below: 

Account: Curbside Technologies (mid-market retail logistics)
Deal: CRB-2029-0427
Current ARR run-rate: $460k
Request: One-time credit to offset Q2 overage; term-reset to calendar-year billing; SLA addendum to 99.95% for 12 months.
Proposed concession (requires exec approval):
- One-time credit: $40,000 (to be applied at signing)
- Term: Reset to 6/1/2029—5/31/2030 with annual billing thereafter
- SLA: Addendum to contract committing to 99.95% availability; standard service credit ladder applies; 30-day ramp window from effective date.

Rationale: Customer is strategic for our retail vertical and is at high risk of churn if we do not provide a bridge. Approving $40k (approx ~8.7% of ARR) secures a 12-month renewal at the higher tier and keeps the relationship intact.

Approvals requested: CFO (pricing concession >$25k) and CEO (non-standard SLA & term reset authority). If approved, Legal will finalize amendment and we will route DocuSign. 

Attachments: proposed_amendment_v3.pdf

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
From: ceo@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, cfo@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EXEC AUTH REQUEST — Approve $40k credit + term reset + SLA addendum for Curbside (deal CRB-2029-0427)

Kimberly — approved.

Two small asks before Legal sends final amendment: 1) make the SLA credit cap explicit (no more than 12% of annual fees in a rolling 12-month period), and 2) include a clause that the one-time credit is forfeited if Curbside terminates within 90 days without cause.

Please coordinate with Legal and Finance to finalize and route DocuSign today — we want this signed before May 15 to minimize churn risk.

— CEO
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: James Reynolds <james.reynolds@curbside.com>
Cc: Olivia Trent <olivia.trent@curbside.com>, procurement@curbside.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Amendment & next steps for Renewal (CRB-2029-0427)

James — great news: leadership approved a $40k one-time credit and the term reset to 6/1/2029—5/31/2030. Legal is updating the draft amendment to include the SLA cap (<=12% of annual fees) and the 90-day forfeiture clause. We'll send DocuSign this afternoon.

Next steps for closing:
1) I will email the updated amendment (DocuSign) — please have an authorized sig sign and return.
2) Procurement to confirm billing details for annual invoices aligned to 6/1.
3) Implementation will schedule the 30-day SLA ramp starting on the effective date.

Thanks for working with us on this. Looking forward to another year of product partnership.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_amendment_v3.pdf
